title: BLACKWALL — open-source VPN client with a route for every app
description: Open-source VPN client for VLESS with REALITY, Trojan, Shadowsocks and VMess. A route for every app and site, DPI bypass, kill switch, no telemetry. Written in Zig for macOS, Windows, Linux and Android.
og_alt: BLACKWALL: every app, its own route
seo_features: A route for every application;A route for every site;DPI bypass;Kill switch;Protection after Disconnect;Reserve servers;Subscriptions and QR codes;VLESS, REALITY, Trojan, Shadowsocks, VMess;UDP through every protocol;Signed automatic updates
eyebrow: Open source · MIT · Written in Zig
sub: A small, fast VPN client for the servers you already have. No Electron, no bundled proxy core, no telemetry.
demo_label: The BLACKWALL window, a live demo
power_label: Turn the VPN on or off (demo)

dl_sub: One file per system, from the latest release. On computers, signed updates arrive on their own.
dl_mac_note: Everything: capture of all traffic, routes for applications and sites, DPI bypass, kill switch, hold from boot.
dl_win_note: Capture through Wintun, routes for applications and sites, DPI bypass, protection after Disconnect, a kill switch on WFP. The first connection installs a system service once.
dl_linux_note: Capture of all traffic, routes for applications and sites, DPI bypass, protection after Disconnect, a strict kill switch on nftables. Kernel 5.7 or newer.
dl_android_note: Capture of all traffic, routes for applications and sites, DPI bypass, subscriptions from a QR code. Android's own Always-on VPN keeps it on from boot.
dl_first_mac: macOS: right-click the app and choose Open. The first connection in TUN mode asks for the administrator password once.
dl_first_win: Windows: SmartScreen, More info, Run anyway. The first connection asks once (UAC) to install the BLACKWALL system service; later releases replace it by themselves.
dl_first_linux: Linux: unpack the archive and run ./install.sh, which adds BLACKWALL to the applications menu, no root needed. The first connection asks for your password once.
dl_first_android: Android: open the APK and allow installation from that source. The first connection asks once whether the app may be a VPN. The APK from GitHub and the app from Google Play are signed differently, so one does not update the other.
